chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: Cab Calloway always paid and musicians sent money home
summary: Milt says Cab never missed a payment and would advance money so musicians could provide for their families.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Who didn't, man? How could you survive out there?
That's right. So you're out there...
When you're away... I don't know anybody out there on that road who was in that band that didn't send that money home, though. Did you?

They all provided. I mean, there isn't a man out there that lost his wife or his family because they religiously didn't send that money home. Because everybody knew you worked with Cab, you got to get paid, he's got a reputation. He never mis-paid nobody who ever worked for him. They'd never say that he missed a payment. Did they, Danny?
No-no. He don't know nothin' about that.

You got paid. So everybody, regardless of what you did or whatever developments you got into, including getting drunk... And Lord knows I did. And I could borrow money. I was three weeks behind in my salary sometimes. Because if I threw that money away, I'd better get some money to send home. And you could get some more. He'd give it to you.
Yeah, it the thing with security there, man.
